card.name: Punctuation ending an avoid-or-don't instruction
card.fires_on: Punctuation or a linking word (; , . as of) right after a clause that tells the reader to avoid, not use, or not give something. It sits where an exception, alternative or reason is about to follow.

modes.label: Break after an avoid instruction
modes.description: A semicolon, comma or period closes an 'avoid use with X' or 'do not give by route Y' clause.
modes.example: Avoid use with VIZIMPRO<<;>> use locally-acting antacids or

modes.label: Linking word in a warning
modes.description: A word such as 'as' or 'of' follows a prohibition or warning and leads into a reason.
modes.example: Avoid balloon releases<< as>> the balloons can land anywhere.

modes.label: Co-administration restriction
modes.description: The word co-administration is cut partway through in a drug interaction warning.

card.writes: It seems to steer the next words toward exceptions or alternatives, and away from words like 'carefully' or 'only if'.
card.plain: It marks the point just after a 'don't use this' instruction, where a workaround or reason usually comes next.
